## Purpose

`summaryBiologicalVar()` gives a quick overview of the biological variables
(BV table) in an RDBES Data Object. For one measured variable — for example
`Age`, `Length`, `WeightLive`, `Sex` or `Maturity` — it counts how many
individuals were measured at each value, split by a chosen grouping field
and restricted to the selected year(s).

The result can be returned as:

- a **table** of counts (`outputType = "table"`),
- a **bar plot** of counts, faceted by the grouping field (`outputType = "plot"`),
- optionally, a **box plot with summary statistics** (`statistics = TRUE`).

## Packages

```{r packages}
library(RDBEScore)
library(RDBESvisualise)
```

## Preparing the data

The function expects a validated RDBES Data Object containing at least the
`SA`, `DE`, `SD`, `FM` and `BV` tables. Create it from an RDBES download with
`RDBEScore::createRDBESDataObject()`:

```{r data}
data <- RDBEScore::H8ExampleEE1
```

The object is validated inside the function
(`RDBEScore::validateRDBESDataObject(strict = TRUE)`), so an invalid object
stops with an informative error before any summarising is done.

It is worth checking which variables and years are present before calling
the function:

```{r explore}
unique(data$BV$BVtypeMeas)   # measured variables available for `var`
unique(data$DE$DEyear)       # years available for `year`
```

## Arguments

| Argument     | Description |
|--------------|-------------|
| `data`       | RDBES Data Object (masterTable with SA, DE, SD, FM, BV). |
| `verbose`    | `TRUE` prints informative messages from the RDBEScore helpers. Default `FALSE`. |
| `var`        | One or more biological variables, matching a value of `BVtypeMeas` (e.g. `"Age"`). |
| `by`         | One or more fields used to split the data, e.g. `"SDctry"` or `"DEhierarchy"`. |
| `year`       | One or more years to keep (filters on `DEyear`). |
| `outputType` | `"table"` or `"plot"`. |
| `statistics` | `TRUE` adds a box plot and a statistics table. Default `FALSE`. |
| `bins`       | Number of bins in histograms. Default is 20.|

## How it works

1. **Validation** – the RDBES Data Object is checked with
   `validateRDBESDataObject()`.
2. **Argument checks** – if `var` is not found in `BVtypeMeas` the function
   stops and lists the variables that are available. Years in `year` that are
   not in `DEyear` produce a warning (not an error).
3. **Filtering** – the object is filtered to the requested years with
   `filterRDBESDataObject(killOrphans = TRUE)`, so records no longer linked
   to a kept design row are removed.
4. **Linking** – `getLinkedDataFromLevel()` attaches each BV record to the
   value of the `by` field it belongs to.
5. **Binning** – for `WeightLive`, values are grouped into 20 intervals so the
   plot stays readable. Other variables are used as they are.
6. **Counting** – the number of individuals (`nIndividuals`) is counted for
   each combination of `by` and `BVvalueMeas`.

## Examples

### Age by country, as a table

```{r table}
summaryBiologicalVar(
  data,
  verbose = FALSE,
  var = "Age",
  by = "SDctry",
  year = 2025,
  outputType = "table",
  statistics = FALSE
)
```

Each row gives the number of individuals of a given age for one country.

### Age by country, as a plot

```{r plot}
summaryBiologicalVar(
  data,
  verbose = FALSE,
  var = "Age",
  by = "SDctry",
  year = 2025,
  outputType = "plot",
  statistics = FALSE
)
```

The plot has one panel per value of `by`; the x axis shows the values of
`var` and the y axis the number of individuals.

### Several years and a hierarchy split

```{r years}
summaryBiologicalVar(
  data,
  var = "Length",
  by = "DEhierarchy",
  year = c(2023, 2024, 2025),
  outputType = "plot",
  statistics = FALSE
)
```

If one of the years is missing from the data, a warning names it and the
summary is built from the years that are present.

### Adding summary statistics

```{r stats}
summaryBiologicalVar(
  data,
  var = "Age",
  by = "SDctry",
  year = 2025,
  outputType = "plot",
  statistics = TRUE
)
```

With `statistics = TRUE` a box plot of the counts (mean marked with a cross)
is drawn above a table of the underlying data.

## Example output on simulated data

The chunks in the *Examples* section need an RDBES export, so they are not
run when the vignette is built. To show what the output looks like, the
chunks below build a small **simulated** count table with the same
structure as the one `summaryBiologicalVar()` creates internally
(one row per `by` value and `BVvalueMeas`, with `nIndividuals`), and draw
it with the same ggplot2 code the function uses. The numbers are not real
RDBES data.

```{r sim-data, eval = TRUE}
library(ggplot2)
set.seed(42)

ages <- 0:10
countries <- c("DK", "PL", "SE")
peak <- c(DK = 3, PL = 4, SE = 5)

simCounts <- do.call(rbind, lapply(countries, function(ctry) {
  data.frame(
    SDctry = ctry,
    BVvalueMeas = factor(ages, levels = ages),
    nIndividuals = rpois(length(ages),
                         lambda = 120 * dnorm(ages, peak[ctry], 2) * 5 + 2)
  )
}))
head(simCounts)
```

### Bar plot (`outputType = "plot"`)

```{r sim-plot, eval = TRUE, fig.height = 4}
ggplot(simCounts, aes(x = BVvalueMeas, y = nIndividuals)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = colourPalette[2], color = "black") +
  labs(title = "Number of individuals by Age and SDctry",
       x = "Age",
       y = "Number of individuals",
       caption = "* Simulated data") +
  facet_wrap(~SDctry) +
  theme_light()
```

### Length distribution split by hierarchy

```{r sim-length, eval = TRUE, fig.height = 4}
lengths <- seq(10, 40, by = 1)
simLength <- data.frame(
  DEhierarchy = "1",
  BVvalueMeas = factor(lengths, levels = lengths),
  nIndividuals = rpois(length(lengths), 300 * dnorm(lengths, 24, 5) + 1)
)

ggplot(simLength, aes(x = BVvalueMeas, y = nIndividuals)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = colourPalette[2], color = "black") +
  labs(title = "Number of individuals by Length and DEhierarchy",
       x = "Length",
       y = "Number of individuals",
       caption = "* Simulated data") +
  facet_wrap(~DEhierarchy, labeller = label_both) +
  scale_x_discrete(breaks = seq(10, 40, by = 5)) +
  theme_light()
```

### Summary statistics (`statistics = TRUE`)

The box plot summarises the counts per group; the cross marks the mean.

```{r sim-stats, eval = TRUE, fig.height = 4}
ggplot(simCounts, aes(x = SDctry, y = nIndividuals)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = colourPalette[2], color = "black") +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", shape = 4, size = 3) +
  labs(y = "Number of individuals per age") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.title.x = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

aggregate(nIndividuals ~ SDctry, data = simCounts,
          FUN = function(x) c(mean = mean(x), sd = sd(x),
                              median = median(x), IQR = IQR(x)))
```

## Common errors

- **"The given measure type ---> X <--- is not present in the data"** –
  `var` does not match any `BVtypeMeas` value. The message lists the valid
  values; spelling and capitalisation must match exactly.
- **Warning about missing years** – some years in `year` are not in `DEyear`.
  Check `unique(data$DE$DEyear)`.
- **Validation error** – the input is not a valid RDBES Data Object; see the
  RDBEScore documentation on `createRDBESDataObject()`.

## Scope

Tested with hierarchy H1 using 2025 RDBES data (downloaded 2026-10-13).
